title: Rabbi Yonatan ben Amram
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Rabbi Yonatan ben Amram (a student of Rabbi). In Bava Batra 8a it is related that Rabbi opened his storehouses in years of drought and said, "Let masters of Scripture enter," etc., but not an ignoramus. Yonatan ben Amram pushed his way in and entered, and when he asked him whether he had studied Scripture or Mishnah, he said to him: No. [Rabbi:] If so, by what merit shall I sustain you? He said to him: Rabbi, sustain me as a dog and as a raven. He sustained him. Rabbi sat and was distressed, and said: Woe is me, that I have given my bread to an ignoramus.

His son Rabbi Shimon said to him: Perhaps it is Yonatan ben Amram, your student, who does not wish to derive benefit from the honor of the Torah all his days? They checked and found it so. Then Rabbi said: Let everyone enter. And in Avodah Zarah 36b, Rabbi Zeira said: I endured great distress at the side of Rabbi Assi, and Rabbi Assi at the side of Rabbi Yochanan, and Rabbi Yochanan at the side of Rabbi Yannai, and Rabbi Yannai at the side of Rabbi Natan (Hyman proposes: Yonatan) ben Amram, and Rabbi Yonatan ben Amram at the side of Rabbi.

(The Tosafot wrote that they were all in the days of Rabbi, and Hyman takes their intent, without doubt, to be from Rabbi Yochanan onward, since Rabbi Assi and Rabbi Zeira are known to have been later.) And there remains to us from him only a single halakhah, in Chagigah 20a: Rabbi Yonatan ben Amram said: His Sabbath garments were exchanged for weekday garments and he put them on; they became impure.

notes.text: The famine story preserves the initial exclusion, the refusal to use Torah’s honor for support and the subsequent admission of everyone. Hyman’s Natan/Yonatan correction and his qualified reading of Tosafot’s chronology remain his own.

Bava Batra 8a directly preserves the admission of everyone after Shimon identifies the student’s refusal to benefit from Torah’s honor. The consulted Tosafot Avodah Zarah 36b expressly says that all were in Rabbi’s time; Hyman’s restriction to Yochanan onward is his interpretation of that statement, not wording in the consulted gloss.
